---
title: "Calorimetry and thermal assessment"
subtitle: "Paired absorption-heat data, fit membership and the remaining high-temperature bias"
---

::: {.callout-warning}
Heat values are direct paired-state total-enthalpy comparisons on the retained
thermal reference. They do not by themselves validate an absorber model. They
were calculated on the superseded Engine `8438ce5f` (wheel `40fba7cf`) with
parameter file `568f7a5f…`, whose coefficients equal the adopted record's. The
pinned Engine provides reference temperature actions
([ePC-SAFT #84](https://github.com/tannerpolley/ePC-SAFT/issues/84)) and
record-anchored total enthalpy
([ePC-SAFT #138](https://github.com/tannerpolley/ePC-SAFT/issues/138)), but
the MEA heat calculation has not been rebuilt on them
([MEA #96](https://github.com/tannerpolley/MEA-Thermodynamics/issues/96)).
:::

# Question

Does the exploratory nine-species bundle reproduce absorption heat across
loading and temperature, and which heat observations were actually allowed to
influence the reaction-temperature fit?

# Starting point and strategy

The calorimetry preparation reads the canonical MEA observation table and
records the preceding endpoint for each finite-loading interval with the same
source, temperature, concentration and run. The retained partition contains
66 Kim–Svendsen 40/80 °C calibration intervals, 20 Kim–Svendsen 120 °C
holdout intervals and 27 Kim et al. 2014 model-selection comparison rows.

Only six 40/80 °C intervals entered the reaction-temperature objective. The
120 °C block remained outside that fit, and Kim 2014 was comparison evidence.
The selected-JSON replay uses one reaction-consistent conserved gauge, Engine
residual enthalpy and an explicit zero-vapor/ideal-CO₂-feed reconstruction.

# Numerical result

::: {.parameter-table .numeric-table}
| Cohort | Intervals | RMSE (kJ mol⁻¹ CO₂) | Bias (kJ mol⁻¹ CO₂) |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| Kim–Svendsen 40/80 °C calibration | 66 | 11.8497 | −2.3 |
| Kim–Svendsen 120 °C holdout | 20 | 31.1500 | −18.8 |
| Kim 2014 comparison | 27 | 10.7128 | — |
:::

The retained reaction-temperature candidate reduced the corresponding paired
errors from 20.01, 39.30 and 16.84 kJ mol⁻¹ CO₂ to 11.84, 31.15 and 10.71.
The pressure and speciation results were regenerated for the adopted record
on the greenfield Engine; the heat results were not, for the reason above.

# Conclusion and limits

The reaction-temperature adjustment improves 40/80 °C heat agreement and the
120 °C comparison, but the 120 °C under-prediction remains material. Loaded
solution heat capacities and MEA ideal-gas heat capacity are not retained, so
solution heat-capacity behavior is predicted rather than independently
validated. The heat study identifies a remaining thermal discrepancy; it does
not justify refitting every EOS or reaction parameter.
